correctness.rationale: The exact lower-triangular commutator entry (m+d)^(-1)[(m+d)^(-alpha)-m^(-alpha)]t^d gives a positive lag-coefficient series. For alpha<1/2, d^(1+2alpha)a_d is a controlled Riemann sum of integrable g_alpha; alpha=1/2 splits harmonic m≤d and summable m>d giving a_d=(log d+O(1))/d²; alpha>1/2 uses summable domination to get d²a_d→zeta(2alpha). Abelian asymptotics with epsilon=1-t² give the exact coefficients and log-squared transition. Euler's double zeta identities yield the alpha=1 corner. This covers t=0,1 and all alpha>0; finite coefficient tests only corroborate.

final_claim: On complex ell2 for alpha>0 and t∈[0,1], [D_alpha,C_t] is Hilbert–Schmidt; the norm-squared endpoint deficit at epsilon=1-t² has epsilon^(2alpha), epsilon log²(1/epsilon)/2, and epsilon log(1/epsilon) with zeta(2alpha) coefficient in the three alpha ranges split at 1/2. At alpha=1 the endpoint is zeta(3)-3zeta(4)/4.
limitations: Only alpha>0 power diagonals, squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm and 0≤t≤1. No operator norm or general Schatten singular value claim.
